adr.title: Target platform: web / PWA only (no store app)
adr.context: The React app replaces the OutSystems mobile app (Cordova, 21 native plugins in the survey: FCM push, Crashlytics, TouchId, Barcode, Location, SocialSharing, File/FileTransfer/FileViewer, InAppBrowser, PrivacyScreen, ScreenOrientation, Keyboard, LocalNotification, AppLauncher, EventfulDeeplinks, AndroidAppLinks). Options were web first + Capacitor later, Capacitor from the foundation, or web/PWA only.
adr.decision: Web / PWA only (user, 2026-10-14). UI stays HTML/CSS 1:1. Native features go behind adapters in src/lib/device with web equivalents decided per feature in the behaviour inventory (extras group C).
adr.consequences: No app-store build. Per-feature web equivalents to decide: push (Web Push; iOS only for installed PWAs, 16.4+), biometric unlock (WebAuthn), barcode (camera + JS library), share (Web Share API), files (download/open), in-app browser (new tab), deep links (URLs + manifest), crash reporting (web monitoring). PrivacyScreen, orientation lock and keyboard control have no full web equivalent. Service worker (Workbox) comes with production integration, not in the mock phase.

adr.title: Baseline: current stable dependency versions before scaffolding
adr.context: Scaffold pins 2024 versions (React 18.3, Vite 5.4, React Router 6.26, TS 5.6, MSW 2.4, Node 20 which is end of life since 2026-04-30). The app replaces production; nothing is built yet.
adr.decision: Upgrade the baseline before scaffolding (user, 2026-10-14: React 19, Node 24 LTS, current stable Vite, React Router, TypeScript, MSW, test and lint tools). Exact versions are chosen from the npm registry, checked together in a scratch install (typecheck, build, tests), listed for the user, then pinned with dep add.
adr.consequences: The foundation owner adapts scaffold_react_app.py output to the new majors once (router, MSW, test setup). Version list needs the user's acceptance before dep add.

adr.title: Third-party libraries for OutSystems modules and OSUI providers
adr.context: Build screens use Leaflet (BrowseDirectory, CountryDetails), SortableJS (Services), ReactiveHtmlSanitizer (MessageDetail, Notifications, Photobook) and OSUI patterns with provider libraries: Carousel (Splide), DropdownSearch (Virtual Select), RangeSlider (noUiSlider + wNumb). Versions read from TST file headers 2026-10-14.
adr.decision: Same libraries as the original: leaflet 1.9.4, leaflet.markercluster 1.5.3, sortablejs 1.15.7, @splidejs/splide 4.1.3, Virtual Select, noUiSlider + wNumb; dompurify 3 with the sanitizer module's allow lists. BottomSheet, Gallery, GalleryV2 hand-written. User: any library that keeps the UI 1:1 (2026-10-14).
adr.consequences: Exact versions of Virtual Select, noUiSlider, wNumb and dompurify go into the ADR-2 version list for the user; dep add after that list is accepted.

adr.title: Tooling for the API contract (group A) and the component catalog (group D)
adr.context: User chose extras A (OpenAPI contract with OutSystems action names, MSW validates against it) and D (Storybook catalog, CI, docs) on 2026-10-14.
adr.decision: Proposed: openapi-typescript (types from the contract) + openapi-fetch (typed client); Storybook for the shared blocks; CI as a platform-neutral npm run ci script (no platform chosen, git init only when the user asks).
adr.consequences: Packages and versions go into the ADR-2 version list for the user's acceptance; the scaffold gains api/contract generation and a .storybook setup in the foundation.

adr.title: Bookmark sync replaces the local bookmarks in one IndexedDB transaction
adr.context: SynchBookmarks / SynchBookmarksC2 (app start, via Sync_Info_GetMain) run DeleteAll then CreateOrUpdate as two IndexedDB transactions in the original (OutSystems.js deleteAll -> executeTransaction). A screen that reads LocalBookmark between the two steps sees no bookmark (menu shows Bookmark instead of Unmark). On TST the first screen reads before the sync starts; in the clone the first screen loads right after the GetUserInformation step, so its read lands inside the sync (HouseholdDetails default parity, F4a 2026-10-15). Known original race: known-original-bugs.md B5.
adr.decision: Keep the clone's entityService.replaceAll: delete and re-create the bookmark rows in one transaction (app/src/shell/localEntities/entities.ts:230, localBookmarks.ts:200-225). Recommended by the orchestrator; auto-accepted under the user's auto mode (2026-10-15 16:59) and listed for the user's review.
adr.consequences: Deviation from the 1:1 rule (bugs included): a read during the sync now sees either the old or the new rows, never none. No visible change on TST timing. Revert = two transactions again plus a timing exemption on HouseholdDetails default.

adr.title: PWA: installable online-first app with a Workbox service worker (vite-plugin-pwa injectManifest)
adr.context: ADR-1 fixes web/PWA only; stack pwa said no service worker in the mock phase. The user decided the PWA plan on 2026-10-16 (migration/pwa/pwa-discussion-plan.md section 7: P1 online-first, P2 injectManifest, P3 caching table 3a, P4 TST manifest values + browser default install prompt, P11 silent update, P13 iOS 16+ degrade, P16 app SW only in non-mock builds). TST manifest fetched (migration/runtime-sources/UBTConnect.pwa-manifest.json). Versions by the stable rule (major line >= 9 months, version >= 60 days, checked 2026-10-16): vite-plugin-pwa 1.3.0 (1.x since 2025-03-29; 2.0.0 is from 2026-10-03, too young; peer vite ^7), workbox-* 7.4.1 (7.x since 2023-05-31; 7.4.1 from 2026-05-04).
adr.decision: Add vite-plugin-pwa 1.3.0 (dev) and workbox-build 7.4.1 (dev); workbox-window, workbox-core, workbox-precaching, workbox-routing, workbox-strategies, workbox-expiration 7.4.1. Own SW file (injectManifest) built and registered only when VITE_USE_MOCKS=false; mock/demo builds keep MSW and unregister a stale app SW. Manifest = TST values (name/short_name Connect 2.0, standalone, theme #1992ab, background #ffffff, TST icons 48-512, start_url and scope /UBTConnect/, portrait), browser default install prompt only. Caching per table 3a: precache hashed bundles + original per-screen CSS + fonts; navigations network-first with the precached index.html fallback; original images cache-first 30 days; never API, signed photos, /bff/*, auth callback, network-ping. Silent update: the new SW waits for the next cold start (no skipWaiting); forced reload only when the API contract version changes (hook ready, wired with the BFF). Offline keeps the original toasts (no offline screen).
adr.consequences: Parity and captures keep blocking service workers; PWA behaviour gets its own Playwright e2e (P14, phase 5). Two build modes to document (mock with MSW, production with the app SW). iOS: no install prompt, separate storage, features degrade without errors. Push, WebAuthn, BFF auth and the barcode scanner come in later phases with their own ADRs.

adr.title: Personal data in IndexedDB: documented exception to stack tokens
adr.context: Stack tokens: never in browser storage. The original (TST) keeps notes, bookmarks, search history, recent searches and Orbit local entities in IndexedDB; the clone does the same (app/src/shell/localEntities, ADR-8). The user decided P10 on 2026-10-16: keep it as the original.
adr.decision: Client entities stay in IndexedDB as in the original. Tokens, PIN and identity secrets are never stored in browser storage (unchanged). When installed, call navigator.storage.persist(); after an eviction, re-sync from the server; clear all local entities on logout. Only the shell stores touch browser storage (rule NO-BROWSER-STORAGE unchanged for routes).
adr.consequences: Personal data at rest on the device, as today in TST; the privacy notice must mention it. Safari may evict data of non-installed sites; every screen must work after an eviction.

adr.title: Vendor the TST BarcodePlugin web scanner (OSBarcodePlugin.js) for PWA scanning
adr.context: PWA decision P7 (user, 2026-10-16): vendor the TST scanner. The original BarcodePlugin, without Cordova and with navigator.mediaDevices, loads OSBarcodePlugin.js (html5-qrcode + ZXing web scanner, BarcodeDetector when supported, rear camera) (migration/runtime-sources/BarcodePlugin.controller.js:21-94, 201-203). The clone answers CheckBarcodePlugin 'not available' (OS-PLUG-BARC-0011) and registers a fictional scanner in the mock phase (OrbitAdminEventDetail Q1 = A). Rule: libraries the original ships keep the TST version.
adr.decision: Vendor migration/runtime-sources/BarcodePlugin.OSBarcodePlugin.js unchanged (as ADR-5/7), with its CSS as AddCSSJS injects it, behind a device adapter (src/lib/device, named by ADR-1). Port CheckBarcodePlugin / ScanBarcode web branches 1:1. Production uses the web scanner; dev and demo keep the fictional scanner by default (Q1 = A) and use the web scanner with ?scanner=web.
adr.consequences: Needs HTTPS (or localhost) and camera permission; iOS has no BarcodeDetector, so ZXing decodes. The vendored file is third-party code (html5-qrcode and ZXing, Apache-2.0 per its headers, to verify) with no npm updates; upgrades follow TST.
adr.confirmed: user, 2026-10-17 (explicit review of the auto-accepted ADR)

adr.title: PWA test suite: Playwright PWA e2e and Lighthouse CI (@lhci/cli 0.15.1)
adr.context: PWA decision P14 (user, 2026-10-16): Playwright PWA e2e + manual device matrix + Lighthouse CI; parity keeps blocking service workers. Versions by the stable rule (checked 2026-10-16): @lhci/cli 0.15.1 (0.15 line since 2025-06-09, 0.15.1 from 2025-06-25; bundles lighthouse 12.6.1). playwright 1.62.1 is already allowed.
adr.decision: Add @lhci/cli 0.15.1 (dev) after a scratch install and npm audit (no high or critical). PWA e2e runs with the playwright package already in the stack (no new runner) against the demo build served by its bundled static server and the production build (vite preview): SW registration and scope, install criteria (manifest, icons), offline reload, ping never cached, update flow (new SW waits), no MSW in production, mock-free production. Lighthouse CI runs on the demo build (performance, accessibility, best practices; PWA category removed in Lighthouse 12) with assertion budgets recorded as warnings first.
adr.consequences: CI gets two extra scripts (e2e:pwa, lhci) that need a Chrome; the device matrix stays manual (docs checklist). Budgets start as warnings and are tightened by ADR later.
adr.confirmed: user, 2026-10-17 (explicit review of the auto-accepted ADR)

adr.title: Lighthouse runs through the lighthouse package 13.4.1 instead of @lhci/cli
adr.context: ADR-12 chose @lhci/cli 0.15.1 for Lighthouse CI. Its scratch install fails npm audit with 11 high advisories from its own tree (tmp, extract-zip, basic-ftp/proxy-agent, puppeteer-core, inquirer, bundled lighthouse 12.6.1); 0.15.1 is the newest release (PWA-5T report 2026-10-16). lighthouse 13.4.1 (13.x since 2025-10-10, 13.4.1 from 2026-07-20) passes the stable rule and a scratch audit shows 0 vulnerabilities.
adr.decision: Replace @lhci/cli by lighthouse 13.4.1 (dev), driven by a small Node script (npm run lighthouse) with the ADR-12 scope: demo build served statically, HomeFeed / Search / OrbitLanding at mobile emulation, performance, accessibility, best practices, warning budgets, local filesystem output only (never uploaded).
adr.consequences: No LHCI server or assertion DSL; the script implements the budgets. Same Chrome requirement as the e2e suite.
adr.confirmed: user, 2026-10-17 (explicit review of the auto-accepted ADR)

adr.title: Production service worker served at TST's worker URL /UBTConnect/pwaServiceWorker.js (cutover handover)
adr.context: PWA fact F2 (user, 2026-10-17): TST registers /UBTConnect/pwaServiceWorker.js on scope /UBTConnect/. It is cache-first for every screen path from its precache, and old caches are deleted only by a newer worker (migration/knowledge/pwa-tst-service-worker.md). Browsers re-check the registered script URL; if it answers 404 after cutover, devices keep the cached OutSystems app. P15 decided a same-origin cutover with a service-worker handover. Options: (A) serve our own worker at that URL; (B) a kill switch at that URL, then the new index.html registers /sw.js.
adr.decision: Option A (user, 2026-10-17): production builds serve the app service worker at /UBTConnect/pwaServiceWorker.js with scope /UBTConnect/, instead of /sw.js. Browsers update the existing registration in place on their next update check. On activate, the worker deletes the OutSystems caches (names starting with UBTConnect-).
adr.consequences: Production SW URL and output path change (src/pwa/swRoutes.ts SW_URL, build/pwa.ts, src/sw/sw.ts activate cleanup, tests, docs/guides/pwa.md). The URL must keep answering from cutover on (never 404). The worker file stays under /UBTConnect/, not at the root of the origin shared with ConnectMobile. The demo build is not covered by this ADR (own host). Implementation is phase 5 work.
